arxiv-2005-11588.title: Subgradient Regularized Multivariate Convex Regression at Scale
arxiv-2005-11588.creator: Wenyu Chen, Rahul Mazumder
arxiv-2005-11588.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Wenyu Chen, Rahul Mazumder. We present new large-scale algorithms for fitting a subgradient regularized multivariate convex regression function to n n samples in d d dimensions—a key problem in shape constrained nonparametric regression with applications in statistics, engineering and the applied sciences. The infinite-dimensional learning task can be expressed via a convex quadratic program (QP) with O ⁡ ( n ​ d ) O(nd) decision variables and O ⁡ ( n 2 ) O(n^{2}) constraints.

arxiv-2306-05992.title: Accretion in the Binary System GG Carinae and Implications for B[e] Supergiants 2023 Accretion in the Binary System GG Carinae and Implications for B[e] Supergiants – References
arxiv-2306-05992.creator: Amit Kashi
arxiv-2306-05992.description: Abstract We simulate the hydrodynamics of the wind flow in the B[e] supergiant binary system GG Carinae and obtain the mass accretion rate onto the secondary and the observed lightcurve. We find an inhomogeneous Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion into a curved accretion tail, and confirm that the accretion rate is modulated along the orbit, with a maximum close to periastron.

pmc-11570577.creator: Dalma Tényi, Györgyi Csábi, József Janszky, Róbert Herold, Tamás Tényi
pmc-11570577.description: It has been recognized that subtle, cosmetically insignificant anomalies tend to occur cumulatively in diseases with neurodevelopmental origin. These visible signs of morphogenesis errors are called minor physical anomalies (MPAs), serving as sensitive external markers of abnormal neurodevelopment. After the introduction of the Waldrop Scale, the studies conducted on MPAs in diseases with neurodevelopmental origin gave conflicting results.

pmc-12635969.title: A Twisted-Integrated Multifunctional Fiber Sensor for Real-Time Metabolic Monitoring and Management of Sepsis
pmc-12635969.creator: Sijia Yu, Ying Jiang, Yiyang Liu, Zheyuan Zhou, Ting Liu
pmc-12635969.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Sepsis-induced systemic metabolic dysregulation involves complex interactions between acid–base imbalance and glucose metabolism abnormalities. Traditional metabolic monitoring methods, which rely on intermittent blood sampling, lack sufficient spatiotemporal resolution and fail to capture the dynamic pathological changes in detail. To address this, we present a minimally invasive multifunctional fiber sensor (PGFs) with a twisted integration structure for real-time, simultaneous monitoring of pH and glucose concentrations in sepsis.
